question: What price should a shopkeeper mark on an article, which costs him ₹136, to gain 20% after allowing a discount of 15%?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The relation between **Cost Price (CP)** and **Marked Price (MP)** is given by: **CP/MP = (100 − Discount%)/(100 + Gain%)**.

Substituting the values: 136/MP = (100 − 15)/(100 + 20) ⇒ 136/MP = 85/120.

MP = (136 × 120) ÷ 85.

MP = (136 × 24) ÷ 17 ⇒ 8 × 24 = 192.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹192.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** CP = ₹136, Gain% = 20%, Discount% = 15%.

**Formulas:** SP = CP × (100 + Gain%) ÷ 100 | MP = (SP × 100) ÷ (100 − Discount%).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/436e67649f25d3f0c85fe261ece925993452bbdec40c4e32cb48287bc1ae584a.png] 

⇒ **Selling Price (SP)** = 136 × (120/100) = ₹163.20.

⇒ **Marked Price (MP)** = (163.20 × 100) ÷ (100 − 15).

⇒ MP = 16320 ÷ 85 = ₹192.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹192.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Marked Price & Discount

**Marked Price** is the price printed on the label. **Discount** is always calculated on the MP to arrive at the **Selling Price**.

Markup Percentage

Markup% = [(MP − CP) ÷ CP] × 100. It shows how much higher the MP is relative to the cost.
